02 / 07

Problem Identification / Statement

Existing Operational Issues

  • Manual, inconsistent record-keeping across branches leads to balance errors.
  • No single source of truth for joint account holders and linked accounts.
  • Duplicate or clashing account / transaction IDs during peak processing.
  • Transfers can be posted without a guaranteed debit-credit balance.
  • Withdrawals sometimes processed against inactive or over-drawn accounts.
  • Loan repayments tracked separately from the original repayment schedule.

Problem Statement

"Banks require a centralized, constraint-enforced relational database that keeps customer, account, transaction, transfer, and loan records consistent, auditable, and available in real time — without manual reconciliation."

03 / 07

Scope & Objectives

Scope

  • Conceptual (ER) and logical (relational) design covering all core banking entities.
  • Normalization of the schema up to Third Normal Form (3NF).
  • Implementation-ready schema with primary keys, foreign keys, and integrity constraints.
  • Realistic sample data and SQL queries for reporting and auditing.
  • A small front-end application demonstrating core banking operations.

Out of scope: mobile apps, real-time payment gateways, multi-currency accounts, regulatory certification.

Objectives

  1. Identify major entities, attributes, relationships, and user roles.
  2. Produce a conceptual ER model and convert it into a normalized relational schema.
  3. Enforce key business rules through constraints — unique IDs, balanced transfers, active-account checks, positive amounts.
  4. Populate realistic sample data and validate it with SQL queries and reports.
  5. Build a small front-end app demonstrating CRUD, search, and validation.
  6. Demonstrate data integrity and indexing through systematic testing.
04 / 07

Users & Functional Requirements

Intended Users

  • Customer — views balances, transactions, and statements.
  • Teller / Branch Staff — manages accounts, deposits, withdrawals, and transfers.
  • Loan Officer — originates loans and tracks repayment schedules.
  • Branch Manager — reviews branch-level reports and summaries.
  • Database Administrator — maintains schema integrity and access control.

Functional Requirements

  1. Register customer profiles and open accounts, including joint holdings.
  2. Record deposits, withdrawals, and transfers with balanced debit/credit.
  3. Maintain beneficiaries and apply service charges per account.
  4. Originate loans, generate schedules, and record repayments.
  5. Generate account statements and branch-wise reports.
  6. Enforce unique IDs, positive amounts, and active-account rules.
